strategies.name: Own Chōfu deep

critique.summary: A3's two early baseball podcast host-reads (day 5 and day 20) are the most efficient spend so far, delivering 14.1% reach (P10 13.1%) at $1768 per point versus the benchmark's 6.0% at $2126. Zone-level spend is not paying back: the Chōfu social ads (social:0 and social:4, $2520 each) and street-team days are each credited with about 1% or less of adoption, and A1's Chōfu-heavy plan lags at 12.2% reach for $2032 per point.

findings.finding: The podcast reads on R2C2 (day 5) and Talkin' Baseball (day 20) earn 11.1% and 9.1% of adoption for about $3400 each, which pushes word of mouth to 54.5% and gives the best P10 at 13.1%.

The ten-day city social burst earns 6.5% of adoption for $1800, while social:0 and social:4 earn only 1.0% and 0.7% for $2520 each, and the street days in zone 1 (Insel) and zone 3 (Musashino) earn 0.2% each.
A1 reaches 26.9% in Gaming and sports stars but only 8.6% in Drag Race and Lululemon, so its overall reach of 12.2% (P10 11.3%) costs $2032 per point, barely better than the benchmark's $2126.
Fourteen Chōfu street days ($6300) are each credited with 0.2–0.3% of adoption, and the day-38 and day-40 pop-ups land too late for word of mouth to spread (Kobeya earns 0.9%).

changes.change: In A3, drop social:0 and social:4 ($5040) and use the money for a third baseball podcast host-read before day 15, plus an extension of social:city from 10 to about 20 days.
changes.why: Podcasts and city social earn 6–11% of adoption per $2–3k, while the zone social ads earn under 1% each.

changes.change: Cut all street-team days for zone 1 (Insel) and zone 3 (Musashino), plus the day-40 street days in zones 0 and 4.
changes.why: Each is credited with 0.2% of adoption, and the day-40 visits are too late to seed word of mouth.

changes.change: Move the Kobeya pop-up (popup:6D058F6D) from day 40 to around day 25.
changes.why: Running it earlier lets the 50%+ word-of-mouth share build on it before launch.

changes.change: Add Drag Race/Lululemon-relevant targeting for zone 3 Musashino through a partner rather than street days.
changes.why: This is the weakest district in both plans (8.6–12.2%) despite a 0.575 fit.

Zone-level spend is not paying back: the Chōfu social ads (social:0 and social:4, $2520 each) and street-team days are each credited with about 1% or less of adoption, and A1's Chōfu-heavy plan lags at 12.2% reach for $2032 per point.

e.text: Applying the Critic's notes: move $5,040 of Chōfu ads into a third podcast read and longer city-wide ads.

e.note: Revising: Revise A3: drop the Chōfu zone social ads and the street days on the wharf, in Musashino, and on day 40. Add a third podcast host-read before day 15 (Talkin' Yanks or The Players' Tribune), run city social for about 20 days, move the Kobeya pop-up to around day 25, and add a Musashino partner such as Cafe Sacai. e.note: Writing the launch plan for B1

plan.headline: Baseball podcasts plus Tokyo-wide social reach about 3x the benchmark's natural audience
plan.summary: The bet is two early host-reads on the strongest baseball shows plus a full-run Tokyo social campaign to start word of mouth, while Chōfu events at Kobeya and Trattoria Filo convert the high-fit local base. Qloo taste data shows this audience over-indexes on R2C2 (0.96), Talkin' Baseball (0.94) and Chōfu venues like Trattoria Filo (0.92), all driven by Ohtani, Yamamoto and MLB affinity. The simulation projects about 19.9% reach of the natural audience (18.8%–21.1%), roughly 3.3x the 6.0% benchmark, at $1183 per point versus $2126; this comes from a model built on Qloo taste data, not a guarantee.
